10.1002_adfm.78384: Aqueous Zn batteries are promising for safe and low‐cost large‐scale energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by severe Zn anode instability arising from coupled hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and dendritic electrodeposition, particularly under temperature extremes. Here we report a solvation–interphase coupled strategy enabled by a hydrated eutectic electrolyte formulated from zinc trifluoromethanesulfonate (Zn(OTf) 2 ), ethylene glycol (EG), and an SnF 2 additive (optimized as ZOTF‐16/SF30), which delivers stable Zn electrochemistry over an exceptionally wide temperature window from −40°C to 60°C. Spectroscopic and physicochemical analyses reveal that EG confines H 2 O within a reinforced hydrogen‐bond network and reconstructs the Zn 2+ coordination environment, thereby suppressing active‐water reactivity and mitigating hydrogen evolution and corrosion. Concurrently, SnF 2 programs interfacial chemistry to generate an in situ zincophobic/zincophilic bilayer interphase, wherein the zincophobic component blocks water penetration and parasitic reactions while the zincophilic component homogenizes Zn 2+ flux and nucleation, enforcing uniform Zn deposition and dendrite‐free growth. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit ultrastable cycling for over 2400 h at 1 mA cm −2 . Moreover, Zn||I 2 full cells deliver remarkable long‐term durability over 120 000 cycles, sustaining extended lifetimes at 60°C and −40°C. This work establishes a practical electrolyte‐interphase co‐design blueprint for climate‐resilient aqueous Zn batteries, highlighting hydrated eutectic chemistry as a versatile platform for stabilizing reactive metal anodes.
10.1002_adma.74891: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are central to the global energy transition, dominating the markets for electric vehicles and grid-scale renewable energy storage. However, as LIBs are pushed toward their theoretical energy density limits to meet ever-escalating performance demands, they are confronted with challenges to their intrinsic operational safety and long-term cycling stability. In recent years, protonic species within LIBs have been increasingly recognized as critical drivers of accelerated cell degradation and premature failure. In this contribution, we first recapitulate the diverse sources and generation pathways of protonic species, with a particular emphasis on the chemical and electrochemical oxidation of state-of-the-art carbonate-based electrolytes. Subsequently, we elucidate the proton-mediated failure network and associated self-amplifying proton-regeneration cycle, including electrolyte degradation and proton-driven parasitic interfacial side reactions at both the anode- and cathode-electrolyte interphases. Furthermore, we highlight critical advancements in in situ/operando characterization techniques for elucidating the sources and degradation mechanisms of protonic species, and propose a mitigation framework centered on proton source suppression and proton scavenging strategies. Finally, we pinpoint unresolved challenges and outline prospective research directions in this field. This contribution establishes critical connections between fundamental proton chemistry and failure modes, which will provide key strategic guidelines toward durable and safe high-energy-density LIBs.
10.1002_anie.2060850: Conventional strategies to address sluggish polysulfide conversion and the shuttle effect have primarily focused on interactions between sulfur anions and catalytic centers, while largely neglecting the enrichment and transport of lithium ions at the cathode. Herein, we report a niobium (Nb) atomic catalyst anchored on graphdiyne (Nb‐GDY) that enables a unique dual‐end binding mechanism for the simultaneous regulation of polysulfide conversion and lithium‐ion transport kinetics. Density functional theory calculations reveal pronounced electronic coupling between Nb─S and Li─C pairs, creating synergistic binding sites that immobilize LiPSs while lowering the energy barriers for their transformation. This mechanism is corroborated by x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy and comprehensive in situ characterizations, which demonstrate significantly accelerated electrode kinetics and efficient Li + flux. Consequently, the Nb‐GDY‐based cathode exhibits exceptional high‐rate capability and long‐term durability, achieving a high capacity of 724 mAh g −1 at 10 C and maintaining stable operation over 1200 cycles at 5 C with a low‐capacity decay of 0.025% per cycle. Our research ingeniously combines dual ends binding, activating the synergistic interaction between atoms and the substrate, providing a new concept for the management of multi‐species transport for high energy density Li−S batteries.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.157286: Solid oxide electrolysis (SOEL) systems are expected to operate dynamically under fluctuating renewable power while maintaining lifetime and performance. This work investigates dynamic operation of a modular 10 MW SOEL plant with ten 1 MW modules using a multi-scale framework combining electrochemical, thermal, degradation, lifetime, stack-level multiphysics, and system-level dispatch models under wind power profiles. The results show that temperature gradients during load transients can be avoided by rapid ramping or by reverse-pulse electrolysis–fuel cell (AC:DC) operation during longer ramps. Combined with Potentio-Galvanostatic operation, these strategies also suppress degradation-induced thermal gradients during steady operation. The predicted module lifetime is 4.1 years and can be increased by up to 60% by redistributing operation among modules and cooling idle modules during low-power periods. Introducing ±20% power-consumption offsets between modules reduces unused renewable power from 10.2% to 2.4% and increases the system capacity factor without significant lifetime penalties.
10.1021_acs.estlett.6c00550: Low-micrometer microplastics (<10 μm) have been detected in drinking water, driving growing interest in using pressure-driven membrane filtration to remove these particles and ensure drinking water safety. However, little attention is paid to the fate of microplastics concentrated in the filtration byproduct. In this study, using well-defined polystyrene (PS) and poly(methyl methacrylate) microspheres as model particles, we observed microplastic fragmentation during nanofiltration and the subsequent release of smaller fragments. After operating for 3 h at 20 bar, 67.9 ± 8.0% of the PS spheres in the concentrate, based on particles counted in selected fields of view, were transformed into fractured particles. The characteristic Raman band signals of microplastics were significantly weakened after fragmentation, leading to detection challenges. To address this, a data processing algorithm was developed to identify PS fragments as small as 1 μm. Preliminary statistical analysis reveals that within the tested pressure range, operation time has a stronger influence on fragmentation than pressure magnitude alone and that fragmentation is further governed by the intrinsic mechanical properties of the tested model polymers. This work provides direct evidence that pressure-driven membrane processes induce microplastic fragmentation and highlights the environmental risks associated with the discharge of fragmented microplastics into the concentrate.
10.1021_acsami.5c22566: Recent advances in solution-processed metal halide perovskites recognize precursor solutions as complex colloidal suspensions where additive engineering critically influences crystallization kinetics and film morphology. While additives have been widely reported to suppress trap defects, their roles in regulating the colloidal coordination environment, particularly the bimodal size distribution of the perovskite solution, remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) as a single-molecule multifunctional agent that uniquely reconfigures colloidal suspensions of a perovskite precursor. TFA’s strong electron-withdrawing effect protonates the solvent molecules, shifting solution pH from alkaline to acidic and collapsing bimodal distributions into homogeneous small colloids via dissolution of iodoplumbate aggregates ([PbI m X n ] 2– ). Concurrently, TFA enhances homogeneous nucleation through direct precursor coordination and unifies crystal growth. This dual control yields films with reduced defects and improved crystallinity, achieving a PCE increase from 23.3% to 25.2% with synergistic gains in V OC, J SC, and FF. Our work emphasizes the crucial roles of unifying the colloidal homogeneity of the perovskite precursor solution in advancing the perovskite solar cell performance.
10.1021_acsnano.6c14363: Aprotic lithium-oxygen (Li-O2) batteries suffer from large voltage hysteresis and inferior reversibility, originating from the sluggish redox kinetics of insulating Li2O2. Here, we incorporate Ru atoms into Co nanoparticles encapsulated within carbon nanotubes and induce a phase transition from a face-centered cubic (fcc) to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure to facilitate cathode reaction kinetics. The hcp-RuCo alloy exhibits significant charge redistribution and a downshifted d-band center, promoting LiO2 desorption into the electrolyte and inducing the formation of solution-mediated, sheet-like Li2O2 nanoarrays with rapid charge/mass transport. Notably, it reduces the delithiation energy barrier to drive a kinetically dominant, stepwise, single-electron oxidation pathway (Li2O2 → LiO2 → O2), bypassing the highly polarizing two-electron route upon charging. Consequently, Li-O2 batteries with the hcp-RuCo catalyst achieve remarkably reduced polarization of 0.72 V and ultralong cycle durability without performance decay. This work demonstrates that crystal-phase engineering is a powerful strategy for tuning oxygen electrocatalysis.
